steps.do: If the reason is lost, stolen or fraud_suspected, skip the card-age requirement. For any other reason, call get_current_time and check that at least 14 days have passed from the card's date_issued to today. If not, tell the customer the earliest date the card can be closed (date_issued + 14 days), and do not close it.
steps.quote: These reasons bypass the minimum card age requirement (requirement 6) for security purposes

basis.quote: These reasons bypass the minimum card age requirement (requirement 6) for security purposes
6. Minimum card age: The debit card must have been active for at least 14 days. Calculate this from the date_issued field.

steps.do: Check the closure requirements. (1) The card belongs to the verified user. (2) The card is ACTIVE or PENDING; a FROZEN card goes through cl_unfreeze_first first. (3) cl_txns shows no pending transactions; if any are pending, tell the customer they must wait for all transactions to settle before the card can be closed. (4) No pending refunds. No lookup reads refunds to a card, so ask the customer. If a refund is pending, they must wait for it to process (typically 3-5 business days) or acknowledge in writing that it will be credited to the linked checking account. (5) Card age, from cl_age. If any requirement fails, tell the customer what must be resolved and do not close that card.
steps.quote: 3. Check eligibility requirements. If any requirement is not met, inform the customer what needs to be resolved and do not proceed with closure.

basis.quote: 3. Check eligibility requirements. If any requirement is not met, inform the customer what needs to be resolved and do not proceed with closure.
2. Customer must be the owner of the debit card (verify user_id matches)
3. The debit card must currently be in ACTIVE or PENDING status

4. No pending transactions: The card must not have any pending or processing transactions. If pending transactions exist, inform the customer they must wait for all transactions to settle before the card can be closed.
Transaction status, either 'posted' or 'pending'.
5. No pending refunds: The card must not have any pending refunds.

If pending refunds exist, inform the customer they must wait for the refunds to process (typically 3-5 business days) or acknowledge in writing that the refunds will be credited to the linked checking account instead.

steps.do: A card that is FROZEN (for example, frozen earlier in this conversation) is not in a status that can be closed. Check that its linked checking account is OPEN in r_accounts. Then unfreeze it with unfreeze_debit_card_3893, which makes it active, and close it right away (cl_close). Tell the customer this is done only so the card can be closed permanently. If the unfreeze fails, tell the customer what the reply says and follow action_error.

steps.do: Confirm the card is permanently deactivated and cannot be reactivated. Tell the customer that recurring payments on it must be updated with new payment details, and that a new card can be ordered through the standard process. For fraud_suspected, also advise them to review recent transactions, dispute any unauthorized charges, and change their online banking password.

rules.rule: A card confirmed lost or stolen is closed, not frozen. Only ACTIVE or PENDING cards can be closed, so a frozen card is unfrozen first. A closed card can never be reopened.
rules.quote: Closed cards cannot be reopened - customer must order a new card if needed

rules.rule: When the PIN-lock protocol finds unauthorized transactions, the card is closed.
rules.quote: If unauthorized transactions found: File dispute, close card, order replacement.

done_when: Each card the customer asked to cancel is closed (a frozen card after it is unfrozen), or the customer was told what must be resolved first. The customer was asked whether they want a replacement. For Entry-tier accounts, the closure time is noted. Any error was explained and a transfer was offered.
